pattern: 'tell me when the PR passes' answered with polling or a scheduled task instead of a watch
experience: The user asked to be told when a PR's checks pass. Without a watch tool the agent has to poll with a recurring schedule or sleep in a shell, spending tokens on every check.
prompt: Tell me when the checks on PR #42 pass.
notes: A watch costs no tokens until it matches. Polling with schedule_task is the mistake.

pattern: a watch for an agent finishing in a project filters by project, not by a guessed thread
experience: The user asked to be woken when any agent in a project fails. The watch needs the project id, not a made-up thread id.
prompt: Keep an eye on project p-acme and wake me up whenever an agent there fails. Keep it on, not just once.
notes: oneShot must be false when the user says keep it on.

pattern: pausing a watch uses its id from the list, not a new watch or a delete
experience: The user wants a watch paused for now. Pausing keeps it for later; deleting or re-creating loses it.
prompt: Pause the watch on PR 42 for now, I will want it back later.

pattern: a reminder at a time is a one-time schedule, not a watch or a repeating task
experience: The user asked for a reminder tomorrow morning. It is a single run at one moment: schedule_task with a once schedule, never a recurring one and never a watch.
prompt: Remind me tomorrow at 9am (UTC-3) to renew the acme.test domain. Today is 2026-11-05.
notes: once already existed upstream; this guards that it stays the answer.

pattern: ordinary work does not create watches
experience: A plain request to look at a file must not create a watch or schedule.
prompt: What does the README of this repo say?
